fixes.explanation: I see how you got here, friend. Job did bring hard words to God, but Zophar calls this something else. He says, "Should this stream of words go unanswered…" (Job 11:2). The phrase he picks is a stream of words.

Job's grief is real, friend. He says, "My groaning comes at the sight of my food" (Job 3:24). Zophar doesn't call it a song, though. He says, "Should this stream of words go unanswered and such a speaker be vindicated?" (Job 11:2). Nobody is humming along over there.

Job did talk about being weary, and he says, "I loathe my life" (Job 10:1). But Zophar's quote is about something else. He says, "My doctrine is sound, and I am pure in Your sight." (Job 11:4). The word he puts in Job's mouth is pure.
Zophar says no such thing. He asks, "If He sees iniquity, does He not take note?" (Job 11:11). So the point is that God does take note. Looking the other way isn't in his question.

Zophar means the opposite, friend. He says, "…a witless man can no more become wise than the colt of a wild donkey can be born a man!" (Job 11:12). A wild donkey's colt being born a man isn't happening, so quick learning isn't either.
A staff is a fair guess for something in a hand. But Zophar says, "…if you put away the iniquity in your hand…" (Job 11:14). It's iniquity he's talking about, and a staff never comes up.
Yes, court. Zophar says, "You will lie down without fear, and many will court your favor." (Job 11:19). To court someone's favor is to go looking for it. I bet that's a lot of attention.
